Ryan Getzlaf (born May 10, 1984) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. He played 17 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played his entire NHL career for the Anaheim Ducks. He served as the captain of the Anaheim Ducks from 2010 until his retirement in 2022. Before playing in the NHL, Dubnyk played 4 years with the Calgary Hitmen of the Western Hockey League (WHL). During his time with the Hitmen, he was named to the WHL East first All-Star team in 2003–04 and the WHL East second All-Star team in 2004–05. Getzlaf also played for Team Canada, winning a gold medal with them at the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver and the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi. On April 5, 2022, Getlaf announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey at the end of the season. On April 24, 2022, Getzlaf played his final game in the NHL in a 6-3 loss to the St. Louis Blues.

Ryan Caldwell (born June 15, 1981 in Brandon, Manitoba) is a Canadian ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Schwenninger Wild Wings of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). He has also played for the New York Islanders and Phoenix Coyotes of the National Hockey League (NHL), the DEG Metro Stars, Eisbären Berlin, and Thomas Sabo Ice Tigers of the DEL, and Ässät and Lukko of the SM-liiga. As an amateur he was an All-American defenceman and captained the University of Denver Pioneers to the 2004 NCAA Championship.

Ryan Braun (born November 17, 1983) is a baseball player for the Milwaukee Brewers of Major League Baseball (MLB). He is an outfielder who plays in left field. He started his career as a Major leaguer in 2007 and won the Rookie of the Year award in 2007. He was a National League All Star in 2008, 2009, 2010, and 2011, and was the Most Valuable Player (MVP) in the National League in 2011. Before playing in the major leagues, Braun played college baseball at the University of Miami. The Brewers chose him with the fifth pick in the 2005 MLB draft. Braun is Jewish, and has said, "being Jewish is something I take great pride in". He has been nicknamed "the Hebrew Hammer".
Ryan Brathwaite (born June 6, 1988) is a track and field athlete from Barbados. He won the gold medal in the 110 metres hurdles at the 2009 World Championships in Athletics in Berlin.

Ryan Thomas Gosling (born November 12, 1980) is a Canadian actor, director, musician, singer and writer. He is known for his roles in The Notebook, in Half Nelson, The Big Short, La La Land, Blade Runner 2049 and Barbie. For his role in La La Land, he won a Golden Globe Award. Gosling was born on November 12, 1980 in London, Ontario, Canada. He studied at Cornwall Collegiate, at the Vocational School, and at the Lester B. Pearson High School. He now lives in Los Angeles, California.

Ryan Scott Dempster (born May 3, 1977 in Gibsons, British Columbia) is a Canadian baseball player. As of 2013, he is a pitcher for the Boston Red Sox of Major League Baseball. Dempster was drafted by the Texas Rangers in the 3rd round of the 1995 MLB Draft. On August 8, 1996, the Rangers traded him along with Rick Helling to the Marlins for John Burkett. He made his MLB debut for the Florida Marlins on May 23, 1998. He would play for the Marlins from 1998 to 2002. On July 11, 2002, Dempster was traded to the Cincinnati Reds in exchange for Juan Encarnacion, Wilton Guerrero and Ryan Snare. He played for the Reds from 2002 to 2003. In August 2003, he underwent Tommy John surgery on his right elbow and missed the rest of the season. He was then released by the Reds and was signed by the Chicago Cubs as a free agent on January 21, 2004. He played for the Cubs from 2004 to 2012 and was then traded to the team that drafted him, the Texas Rangers. He only played a year with the Rangers however and signed a two-year contract worth $26.5 million with the Boston Red Sox after the 2012 season. In early June 2009, he released a statement in which he explained the his daughter, Riley Dempster, had DiGeorge syndrome. He released the statement because he wanted to help raise awareness of the genetic disease. When he was asked if his daughter would be able to lead a normal life, he replied, "Yeah, she will. There can be (problems), but so far all the signs are good. There’s a lot of work to do. They say there are 186 symptoms you can have. You just check off ones as you go along". His daughter was able to go home in early June after 2 months in the hospital.

Ryan Callahan (born March 21, 1985 in Rochester, New York) is an American professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Tampa Bay Lightning of the National Hockey League (NHL). He started his hockey career in the Ontario Provincial Junior A Hockey League. He played 3 games with the Syracuse Jr. Crunch and 1 seasons with the Buffalo Lightning. He also played in the Ontario Hockey League (OHL) with the Guelph Storm for 4 seasons. He was drafted by the New York Rangers with the 127th overall pick in the 2004 NHL Entry Draft. He played one season with the Hartford Wolf Pack of the American Hockey League (AHL) before being called up to the Ranger's main roster. On September 12, 2011, Callahan was named the captain of the Rangers. On March 5, 2014, the Rangers traded Callahan along with a 2015 first-round draft pick, and a conditional 2014 second-round pick to the Tampa Bay Lightning for Tampa Bay captain Martin St. Louis.

Ryan James Howard (born November 19, 1979), nicknamed "The Big Piece", is an American former professional baseball first baseman. Howard spent his entire Major League Baseball (MLB) career playing for the Philadelphia Phillies, from 2004 to 2016. He is known for being the fastest player in baseball history to reach 1,000 RBIs, 100 home runs, and 200 home runs. Howard also holds numerous Phillies franchise records. Howard made his MLB debut in 2004. He won the National League (NL) Rookie of the Year Award in 2005 and the NL Most Valuable Player (MVP) Award in 2006. Howard was a three-time NL All-Star (2006, 2009, 2010), and won the Silver Slugger Award, Hank Aaron Award, and the NL Championship Series MVP Award in 2009. Known for his power, Howard is a member of the 50 home run club. He was a two-time NL home run champion (2006, 2008), and became the fastest player to reach both the 100 and 200 home run milestones in MLB history, passing the marks in 2007 and 2009, respectively. He is also tied with Sammy Sosa for the most National League 140 RBI seasons at 3 and the most National League 130 RBI seasons at 4.

Ryan John Campbell (born 7 February 1972) is an Australian former cricketer. He played as a wicket-keeper. Campbell was born in Osborne Park, a suburb of Perth, Western Australia. He represented his home state from 1995–96 to 2005–06. He played for Australia in two One Day Internationals between 2001–02 and 2002–03. He retired from playing after the 2005–06 season. In 2015, Campbell came out of retirement briefly to represent the Hong Kong team in three Twenty20 Internationals. He became a coach and worked with both Durham County Cricket Club and the Dutch national team. In April 2022, while in England, Campbell went into cardiac arrest. He was in intensive care in a coma. He left Royal Stoke University Hospital three weeks later.

Ryan Donato (born April 9, 1996) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins, Minnesota Wild, San Jose Sharks, and Seattle Kraken. Before playing in the NHL, Donato played parts of one season with the South Shore Kings of the United States Premier Hockey League (USPHL), parts of one season with the Omaha Lancers of the United States Hockey League (USHL), and three years with the Harvard Crimson of ECAC Hockey. He was named to the USHL All-USA Hockey First Team in 2015. With the Crimson, he had a lot of success. He finished the 2016–17 season scoring 21 goals and recording 19 assists for 40 points in 36 regular games. For his effort, Donato was named the Ivy-League Players of the Year, the ECAC Hockey Player of the Year and was also named to the ECAC All-Tournament Team, All-ECAC Hockey Second Team, and All-Ivy League First Team. He was named a finalist for the Hobey Baker Award that year as well. The next year, he was named a AHCA East First-Team All-American. He was drafted 56th overall by the Boston Bruins in the 2014 NHL entry draft. On March 18, 2018, he signed a two-year, $2.7 million entry-level contract to join the Bruins. On April 12, 2024, Donato made his NHL debut in a 5–4 overtime loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. He had very productive debut, assisting on goals from Riley Nash and David Krejčí, and also scoring his first NHL goal against Joonas Korpisalo. On February 20, 2019, the Bruins traded Donato along with a 2019 conditional fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for Charlie Coyle. On July 16, Donato signed a two-year, $3.8 million contract to stay with the Wild. On October 5, 2020, the Wild traded Donato to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for a 2021 third-round draft pick. He played one season for the Sharks, scoring 6 goals and recording 14 assists for 20 points in 50 regular games. On September 13, 2021, Donato signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to join the new expansion franchise Seattle Kraken. On October 12, Donato scored the first goal in Kraken franchise history. On July 27, 2022, Donato signed a one-year contract to stay with the Kraken. On July 1, 2023, Donato signed a two-year, $4 million contract to join the Chicago Blackhawks. On March 28, 2025, Donato recorded his first career NHL hat-trick in a 5–3 loss to the Vegas Golden Knights. On June 18, Donato signed a four-year, $16 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. Donato's father Ted also played in the NHL for 13 seasons.

Ryan Greene (born October 21, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Greene played three seasons with the Green Bay Gamblers of United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He helped the Terriers when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Ohio State Buckeyes, Cornell Big Red, and Penn State Nittany Lions. They were eventually defeated by the Western Michigan Broncos 6–2 in the National Championship game of the Frozen Four. He was drafted 57th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On April 13, 2025, he signed a three-year, $950,000 entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. On March 26, Greene made his NHL debut in a 4–3 shootout win against the Montreal Canadiens. On October 15, Greene scored his first NHL goal against Joel Hofer in a 8–3 win against the St. Louis Blues.

Ryan Keyes Hartman (born September 20, 1994) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks, Nashville Predators, and Philadelphia Flyers. He is the first player in the NHL from South Carolina. Before playing in the NHL, Hartman played three seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Plymouth Whalers of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 30th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks of the 2013 NHL entry draft. On November 18, 2013, Hartman signed an three-year, $2.775 entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Rockford IceHogs. On February 13, 2015, Minnesota called him up and Hartman made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the New Jersey Devils. On November 4, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Marko Daňo goal in a 6–5 overtime loss against the St. Louis Blues. On October 12, 2016, Hartman scored his first NHL goal against Jake Allen in a 6–5 overtime loss against the St. Louis Blues. On January 8, 2017, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–2 win against the Nashville Predators. On February 26, 2018, the Blackhawks traded Hartman along with a 2018 fifth-round draft pick to the Nashville Predators in exchange for Victor Ejdsell, a 2018 first-round draft pick, and a 2018 fourth-round draft pick. On July 16, 2018, Hartman signed a one-year contract to stay with the Predators. On February 25, 2019, the Predators traded Hartman along with a 2020 conditional fourth-round draft pick to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for Wayne Simmonds. He scored 2 goals and recorded 4 assists in 19 regular season games with the Flyers. On June 24, 2019, the Flyers traded Hartman to the Dallas Stars in exchange for Tyler Pitlick. He never played a game for the Stars. On July 1, 2019, Hartman signed a two-year, $3.8 million contract to join the Minnesota Wild. On October 7, 2023, Hartman signed a two-year, $3.8 million contract to stay with the Wild. On October 7, 2023, Hartman signed a two-year, $12 million contract to stay with the Wild.

Ryan Paul Jones (born 13 March 1981) is a Welsh international rugby player. He played for Wales from 2004 to 2014. He also played for Ospreys at the Liberty Stadium. Jones was born in Newport, Wales. He was appointed Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 2021. In July 2022, Jones announced he was diagnosed with a rare form of early-onset dementia.

Ryan M. Johnson (born June 14, 1976) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre who is currently a free agent in the National Hockey League. Johnson also played for the Florida Panthers from 1996 to 2000, the Tampa Bay Lightning in 1999 to 2001, another stint with the Florida Panther from 2001 to 2003, the St. Louis Blues from 2002 to 2008, the Vancouver Canucks from 2008 to 2010 and the Chicago Blackhawks in 2010.

Ryan Miller (born July 17, 1980) is an American former ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres, Vancouver Canucks, and St. Louis Blues. On July 1, 2014, Miller signed a three-year, $18 million contract with the Vancouver Canucks. On April 5, 2022, Miller announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey at the end of the season. On May 8, 2021, Miller played his final game in the NHL in a 4-3 loss to the Minnesota Wild. On January 19, 2023, the Buffalo Sabres retired Miller's jersey number #30. NCAA West First All-American Team (2001, 2002) Hobey Baker Memorial Award (Top U.S. Collegiate Player) (2001) Aldege "Baz" Bastien Memorial Award (Outstanding Goaltender – AHL) (2005) Starter for the Eastern Conference in NHL All-Star Game (2007) MVP of the 2010 Olympic hockey tournament Best Goaltender of the 2010 Olympic hockey tournament All-star selection of the 2010 Olympic hockey tournament

Ryan Neil Raburn (born April 17, 1981) is a former baseball player who last played for the Washington Nationals. He previously played for the Detroit Tigers, Cleveland Indians, and Colorado Rockies. He played many positions, but mostly second base and left field.

Ryan David Leaf (born May 15, 1976) is a former American football player. He was a quarterback in the National Football League (NFL) for four seasons. He played for the San Diego Chargers and the Dallas Cowboys between 1998 and 2001. He also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Seattle Seahawks. Leaf had a successful college career at Washington State University. He was a finalist for the Heisman Trophy. He was the second overall pick in the 1998 NFL Draft. The first pick was Peyton Manning. Leaf's professional career was short and interrupted by injuries. During his brief career in the NFL, Leaf was in 25 games and made 21 starts. The sports network ESPN listed Leaf first on their list of the 25 Biggest Sports Flops between 1979-2004. On March 30, 2012 Leaf was arrested on burglary, theft, and drug charges in his hometown of Great Falls, Montana. Four days later, Leaf was arrested again for the same crimes.

Ryan O'Marra (born June 9, 1987) is a Japanese-born Canadian retired professional ice hockey centre. He played a 33 games in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Edmonton Oilers and the Anaheim Ducks. O'Marra was drafted 15th overall in the 2005 NHL Entry draft by the New York Islanders but never played a game with them although he did play 8 games with their AHL farm team, Bridgeport Sound Tigers. O'Marra was born in Tokyo, Japan to Irish Canadian parents. He moved to Canada when he was one year old. On March 26, 2015, O'Marra announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey.

Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (born April 12, 1993 in Burnaby, British Columbia) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was selected by the Edmonton Oilers with the 1st overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft.

Ryan Newman (racing driver) (born 1977) American stock car racing driver Ryan Whitney (actress) (Birth name Ryan Newman) (born 1998), American actress, singer, and model Ryan Dean Newman, American lawyer and former Army captain

Ryan Reaves (born January 20, 1987) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the St. Louis Blues, Pittsburgh Penguins, Vegas Golden Knights, New York Rangers, and Minnesota Wild. Before playing in the NHL, Reaves played parts of 3 seasons with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). During his time with the Wheat Kings, Reaves served as one of their alternate captains. He was drafted 156th overall overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2005 NHL Entry Draft. On October 11, 2010, Reaves made his NHL debut in a 5-1 win against the Anaheim Ducks. During the game, Reaves fought Kyle Chipchura and received a game misconduct. On January 12, he scored his first NHL goal in a 7-4 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On June 23, 2017, the Blues traded Reaves along with a second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Oskar Sundqvist and a first-round pick. During his time with the Penguins, Reaves scored 4 goals for them. On February 23, 2018, the Penguins traded Reaves to the Vegas Golden Knights in a three-way trade that also included the Ottawa Senators. Reaves was successful in Vegas. He helped the team reach for the 2018 Stanley Cup Finals after scoring the series-winning goal against the Winnipeg Jets. On July 29, 2021, the Golden Knights traded Reaves to the New York Rangers in exchange for a third-round draft pick. On November 23, 2022, the Rangers traded Reaves to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for a fifth-round draft pick. On July 1, 2023, Reaves signed a three-year, $4.05 million contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs. On November 16, 2024, Reaves illegally checked Edmonton Oilers defenseman Darnell Nurse in the head and was given a five-game suspension.

Ryan Lindgren (born February 11, 1998) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs, Florida Panthers, Dallas Stars, and Seattle Kraken. Before playing in the NHL, Lindgren played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one season with the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was drafted 49th overall by the Boston Bruins in the 2016 NHL entry draft. He never played a game for the Bruins. On February 25, 2018, the Bruins traded Lindgren along with Matt Beleskey, Ryan Spooner, a 2018 first-round draft pick and a 2019 seventh-round draft pick to the New York Rangers in exchange for Rick Nash. On March 17, Lindgren signed a three-year, $3.3 million entry-level contract to join the Rangers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. On January 15, 2019, the Rangers called him up and Lindgren made his NHL debut in a 6–2 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On October 29, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Adam Fox goal in a 4–1 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On November 10, Lindgren scored his first NHL goal against Sam Montembeault in a 6–5 shootout loss against the Florida Panthers. On May 10, 2021, Lindgren signed a three-year, $9 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On March 1, 2025, the Rangers traded Lindgren along with Hank Kempf and Jimmy Vesey to the Colorado Avalanche in exchange for Juuso Pärssinen, Calvin de Haan, and both a 2025 second and fourth-round draft pick. He played 18 regular season games with the Avalanche, scoring 2 goals and 1 assist. He also played 7 playoffs games with them and recorded 3 assists. On July 1, 2025, Lindgren signed a four-year, $18 million contract to join the Seattle Kraken. Lindgren's brother Charlie is also professional hockey player for the Washington Capitals. Bryan died on July 6, 2022.

Ryan O'Reilly (born February 7, 1991) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. He has also played for the Colorado Avalanche, Buffalo Sabres, St. Louis Blues, and Toronto Maple Leafs. Outside of the NHL, O'Reilly played for Metallurg Magnitogorsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). O'Reilly is a one-time Stanley Cup champion in 2019. He is also a one-time Lady Byng Memorial Trophy winner, one-time Conn Smythe Trophy winner, and a one-time Frank J. Selke Trophy winner. O'Reilly is a three-time All-Star, being named one in 2016, 2019, and 2020. Before playing in the NHL, O'Reilly played parts of one season with the Erie Otters of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 33rd overall by the Colorado Avalanche in the 2009 NHL entry draft. On March 31, 2014, O'Reilly signed a two-year, $1.535 million entry-level contract to join the Avalanche. On October 1, 2009, O'Reilly made his NHL debut in a 5–2 win against the San Jose Sharks. During the game, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Cody McLeod goal. On October 15, he scored his first NHL goal against Carey Price in a 3–2 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On February 28, 2013, O'Reilly was going to sign a two-year, $10 million contract to join the Calgary Flames but the Avalanche matched the offer sheet and he stayed with the Avs. On June 24, 2014, the league awarded O'Reilly with the Lady Byng Memorial Trophy for showing the best sportsmanship and having gentlemanly conduct during the season. On July 23, O'Reilly signed a two-year, $12 million contract to stay with the Avalanche. On June 26, 2015, the Avalanche traded O'Reilly along with Jamie McGinn to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Nikita Zadorov, Mikhail Grigorenko, J. T. Compher, and a 2015 second-round draft pick. On July 3, O'Reilly signed a seven-year, $52.5 million contract to stay with the Sabres. On July 1, 2018, the Sabres traded O'Reilly to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for Patrik Berglund, Vladimír Sobotka, Tage Thompson, a 2019 first-round draft pick, and a 2021 second-round draft pick. On November 6, O'Reilly recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–1 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. He helped the Blues when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Winnipeg Jets, Dallas Stars, and San Jose Sharks. They went on to defeat the Boston Bruins four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Blues franchise history. O'Reilly was very productive leading up to and during the playoffs. He recorded 23 points in the playoffs, which set a Blues record for most points in the playoffs. After winning the Stanley Cup, O'Reilly was awarded the Conn Smythe Trophy for being the most valuable player in the playoffs. On June 19, 2019, he was awarded with the Frank J. Selke Trophy for being the best defensive forward that season. On December 23, 2020, the team announced O'Reilly as the 23rd captain in Blues franchise history. On February 17, 2023, the Blues traded O'Reilly to the Minnesota Wild in exchange for Josh Pillar. However, he never played a game with the Wild and he was traded the same day to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a 2025 fourth-round draft pick. He played 13 regular season games, scoring 4 goals and recording 7 assists, as well as, 11 playoff games where he scored 3 goals and recorded 6 assists. On July 1, 2023, O'Reilly signed a four-year, $18 million contract to join the Nashville Predators.

Ryan Poehling (born January 3, 1999) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Montreal Canadiens, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Philadelphia Flyers. Before playing in the NHL, Poehling played nine regular season games with the Lincoln Stars of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the St. Cloud State Huskies of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Huskies, he was named to the All-NCHC First Team. He was drafted 25th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 2017 NHL entry draft. On March 31, 2019, Poehling signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Canadiens. On April 6, 2019, Poehling made his NHL debut in a 6–5 shootout win against the Toronto Maple Leafs. During the game, Poehling recorded his first NHL hat-trick. He became the first Canadien to do so since January 14, 1943 when Alex Smart last achieved the feat. After the game, he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Laval Rocket. He spent the next few seasons playing between Montreal and Laval. On August 27, 2021, Poehling signed a two-year contract to stay with the Canadiens. On July 16, 2022, the Canadiens traded Poehling along with Jeff Petry to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Mike Matheson and a 2023 fourth-round draft pick. He scored 7 goals and recorded 7 assists in 53 regular season games for the Penguins. On July 1, 2023, Poehling signed a one-year, $1.4 million contract to join the rival Philadelphia Flyers. On January 27, 2024, Poehling signed a two-year, $3.8 million contract to stay with the Flyers. On June 23, 2025, the Flyers traded Poehling along with 2025 second-round draft pick, and a 2026 fourth-round draft pick to the Anaheim Ducks in exchange for Trevor Zegras. On March 6, 2026, Poehling signed a four-year, $15 million contract to stay with the Ducks.

Ryan Reeves (born November 10, 1981 in Las Vegas, Nevada) is an American professional wrestler. He formally wrestled for the WWE under the ring name Ryback. He was formerly known under the ring name Skip Sheffield and was a former member of the wrestling stable, The Nexus. On November 24th, Ryback would tweet on X saying that if Cm punk returned at wwe’s PLE Survivor series in Chicago he would retire from professional wrestling. A day later Cm punk would shockingly return at survivor series thus putting an end to rybacks career. PWI Feud of the Year (2010) - The Nexus vs. WWE PWI Most Hated Wrestler of the Year (2010) - as a member of The Nexus He was ranked #218 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500. (2010) He was ranked #112 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500. (2012) Slammy Award for the Shocker of the Year (2010) - The debut of The Nexus

Ryan White (born March 17, 1988) is a retired Canadian professional ice hockey center who previously played for the Montreal Canadiens, Philadelphia Flyers, Arizona Coyotes and Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). White spent four seasons, from 2004–05 to 2007–08, in the Western Hockey League with the Calgary Hitmen. He was drafted by the Montreal Canadiens in the third round, 66th overall, in the 2006 NHL Entry Draft. Following his WHL career, White was assigned to the Canadiens' minor league affiliate, the Hamilton Bulldogs of the American Hockey League (AHL), where he recorded 29 points in 80 games as a rookie in 2008–09. White made his NHL debut in a call-up with the Montreal Canadiens on November 5, 2009 against the Boston Bruins, recording an assist. He was called up once again for a game against the Ottawa Senators the following month on December 8. White played the entirety of the first period before being pulled from the game after the NHL noticed he was playing, despite the Canadiens not having properly reported his call-up to the league before the 5 p.m. deadline.

Ryan Stanton (born July 20, 1989, in St. Albert, Alberta) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He played for the Vancouver Canucks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He also played for the Washington Capitals and Chicago Blackhawks. Before he played in the AHL and NHL, Stanton played 4 seasons in the Western Hockey League with the Moose Jaw Warriors. On March 12, 2010, the Chicago Blackhawks signed Stanton as a free agent. He played his first game with the IceHogs on March 6, 2010. Stanton was called up to the Blackhawks roster on April 26, 2013. On September 30, 2013, Stanton was claimed off of waiver by the Vancouver Canucks.

Ryan Tandy (20 September 1981 – 28 April 2014) was an Australian professional rugby league player. He played as both a prop and second row from 2003 until 2011. During his career, he played for the St. George Illawarra Dragons, South Sydney Rabbitohs, Wests Tigers, Melbourne Storm and the Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs in the National Rugby League (NRL). He also played for Hull Kingston Rovers in the European Super League. He represented Ireland from 2006 until 2008. He was banned from playing professional rugby league due to a match fixing scandal. Born in Wollongong, New South Wales, Tandy was found dead of an apparent drug overdose on 28 April 2014 at his parents' home in Saratoga, New South Wales, aged 32.

Ryan VandenBussche (born February 28, 1973) is a Canadian retired professional ice hockey right winger. He played a career total of 9 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the New York Rangers, Chicago Blackhawks, and Pittsburgh Penguins. He was known for his pugilistic skills. Before playing in the NHL, VandenBussche played 2 seasons with the Cornwall Royals of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted with the 173rd overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 1992 NHL Entry Draft. He spent most of his first seasons between the OHL and the American Hockey League (AHL) with the St. John's Maple Leafs, Springfield Indians, and Binghamton Rangers. On August 22, 1995, he signed a contract with the New York Rangers after he became an unrestricted free agent. After he spent two seasons in the AHL with the Rangers AHL-affiliate team, the Binghamton Rangers, VandenBussche made his NHL debut on December 13, 1996 in a 3-0 win against the Buffalo Sabres. After 27 games with the Rangers over 2 seasons, the Rangers traded VandenBussche to the Chicago Blackhawks for Ryan Risidore on March 24, 1998. With the Blackhawks, VandenBussche played 263 games over 7 years with them. On July 12, 2004, he signed a contract with the Pittsburgh Penguins as an unrestricted free agent. He only played 20 games with the Penguins before he was signed for a try-out by Jokerit of the SM-liiga on September 25, 2006. He signed with the New Mexico Scorpions of the Central Hockey League (CHL) as a player/coach on November 5, 2006. On January 17, 2007, he announced that he was retiring from playing professional hockey because of medical reasons. During his career, VandenBussche was mainly known as an enforcer. He is known for ending the career of Nick Kypreos during a fight in a pre-season game in September 1997. After retiring, he decided to sell real estate with his wife Lisa, and under the direction of his father Ron, in Norfolk County. On July 3, 2006, VandenBussche was charged with three counts of assaulting police and one count of uttering a death threat after a fight at a bar in Turkey Point. He was later cleared of the charges.

Ryan Shay, born May 4, 1979 – dead 3 November 3, 2007 was an US professional long-distance runner. He was born in Ypsilanti, Michigan, USA. He attended the University of Notre Dame. He was married to Alicia Craig, who was also an American distance runner. He won several USA championships titles.
Ryan William Walter (born April 23, 1958) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre who played 15 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL).

Ryan Strain (born 2 April 1997) is an English-born Australian soccer player. He plays for St Mirren in the Scottish Premiership and for the Australia men's national soccer team (nicknamed the "Socceroos").

Ryan Alexander Borden Smyth (born February 21, 1976) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of 19 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Edmonton Oilers, New York Islanders, Colorado Avalanche, and Los Angeles Kings. Smyth is a one-time All-Star, being named to the NHL ones in 2007. Internationally, Smyth played for Canada. He won a gold medal them at the 2002 Winter Olympics. Since retiring, Smyth became an owner of the Spruce Grove Saints of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL). Before playing in the NHL, Smyth played parts of four seasons with the Moose Jaw Warriors of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with the Warriors. He was named to the WHL East Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 6th overall by the Edmonton Oilers in the 1994 NHL entry draft. On January 22, 1995, Smyth made his NHL debut in a 4–3 win against the Los Angeles Kings. On November 24, he scored his first career NHL goal against Trevor Kidd in a 5–2 win against the Calgary Flames. He played 6 games with their AHL-affiliate Cape Breton Oilers, scoring 6 goals and recording 5 assists for 11 points. He finished the 1996–97 season with career-bests in 39 goals and recording 61 points. He also tied Wayne Gretzky for most powerplay goals scored for the Oilers. On August 14, 2003, Smyth signed a two-year contract to stay with the Oilers. The 2003–04 season ended well for Smyth and he was very productive during it. He finished the season by scoring 23 goals and recording 36 assists for 59 points which was the second straight season where he led the team in scoring. Smyth served as an alternate captain for the team and also served as their captain when Jason Smith was injured. He helped the Oilers when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Detroit Red Wings, San Jose Sharks, and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim. They went on to be defeated by the Carolina Hurricanes four games to three in the Final. On October 12, 2006, Smyth scored a hat-trick in two minutes and one second which broke Gretzky's record for fastest hat-trick by an Oiler. On February 27, 2007, the Oilers traded Smyth to the New York Islanders in exchange for Robert Nilsson, Ryan O'Marra, and a 2007 first-round draft pick. Smyth did not want to be traded from Edmonton and gave a tearful farewell to Oilers fans for supporting him. He played 18 regular season games with the Islanders, scoring 5 goals and recording 10 assists for 15 points. On July 1, 2007, Smyth signed a five-year, $31.2 million contract to join the Colorado Avalanche. On January 18, 2009, Smyth scored his 300th NHL career goal in in a 6–2 win over the Calgary Flames. Smyth's teammate Milan Hejduk also scored his 300th goal in the same game. On July 3, 2009, the Avalanche traded Smyth to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Tom Preissing, Kyle Quincey, and a 2010 fifth-round draft pick. On November 6, 2010, Smyth played in his 1,000 NHL game in a 4–1 over the Nashville Predators. During the game, he scored a goal against Pekka Rinne. On June 26, 2011, the Kings traded Smyth back to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Colin Fraser and a 2012 seventh-round draft pick. This came after Smyth expressed to the Kings that he desired to play his final season with the Oilers. On March 6, 2014, Smyth broke Wayne Gretzky's record to become the Oilers all-time power-play goal-scorer. On April 11, 2014, Smyth announced that he was retiring from playing professional ice hockey. Smyth's older brother Kevin also played 58 games for the Hartford Whalers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Smyth is a Christian.

Ryan James Wedding (born September 14, 1981) is a Canadian alleged drug lord and former Olympic snowboarder. Wedding competed for Canada at the 2002 Winter Olympics in Salt Lake City, Utah. He participated in the men's parallel giant slalom event and finished in 24th place. He decided to retire from snowboarding after the Olympics. After retiring, Wedding started to find himself in legal trouble. In 2006, his Vancouver property Eighteen Carrot Farms was raided by Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) and they seized $10 million worth of cannabis, a shotgun, and some ammunition. In 2008, Wedding was arrested for trying to buy cocaine from a United States government agent and he was convicted in 2010, sentenced to four years in prison. During his time in prison, Wedding started to make connection with other criminals and made plans to expand his drug empire. On October 17, 2024, the United States Department of Justice announced that they were charging Wedding with multiple offenses including leading a criminal organization, drug trafficking, three counts of murder, and one attempt to commit murder. Authorities claim that when Wedding was released from prison, he went to Mexico and joined the Sinaloa Cartel, which is the largest drug cartels in Mexico. He rose the ranks and became one of the highest-ranking members of the cartel. On March 6, 2025, Wedding was added to the FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list. On January 22, 2026, Wedding turned himself into authorities and he was arrested in Mexico.

Ryan Winterton (born September 4, 2003) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Winterton played two seasons with the Hamilton Bulldogs and one season with the London Knights of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 67th overall by the Seattle Kraken in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On July 13, 2022, Winterton signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Kraken. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Coachella Valley Firebirds. On November 9, 2023, the Kraken called him up and Winterton made his NHL debut in a 4–3 win against the Colorado Avalanche. On November 29, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Brandon Tanev goal in a 4–2 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On November 5, 2025, Winterton scored his first NHL goal against Yaroslav Askarov in a 6–1 loss against the San Jose Sharks. On February 24, 2026, Winterton signed a three-year, $2 million contract to stay with the Kraken.

Ryan Richard Ufko (born May 7, 2003) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Ufko played two seasons with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the UMass Minutemen of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Minutemen, he won the Len Ceglarski Award for best sportsmanship. He was also name a AHCA East First Team All-American and was named to the All-Hockey East Rookie Team, All-Hockey East First Team, and All-Hockey East Second Team. He was drafted 155th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On March 29, 2024, Ufko signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On December 19, 2015, the Predators called him up and Ufko made his NHL debut in a 7–3 loss against the Utah Hockey Club. On March 5, 2026, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Filip Forsberg goal in a 6–3 win against the Boston Bruins. On March 10, Ufko scored his first NHL goal against Joey Daccord in a 4–2 win against the Seattle Kraken.

Ryan Edward Gaston Strome (born July 11, 1993) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New York Islanders, Edmonton Oilers, New York Rangers, and Anaheim Ducks. Before playing in the NHL, Strome played one season with the Barrie Colts and four seasons with the Niagara IceDogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. With the IceDogs, he was named to the OHL Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 5th overall by the New York Islanders in the 2011 NHL entry draft. On October 4, 2011, Strome signed a three-year, $2.775 million entry-level contract to join the Islanders. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Bridgeport Sound Tigers. On December 14, 2013, the Islanders called him up and Strome made his NHL debut in a 1–0 overtime loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On December 20, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Brian Strait goal in a 5–3 win against the New York Rangers. On January 6, 2014, Strome scored his first NHL goal against Kari Lehtonen in a 7–3 win against the Dallas Stars. On September 20, 2016, Strome signed a two-year, $5 million contract to stay with the Islanders. On June 22, 2017, the Islanders traded Strome to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Jordan Eberle. On September 20, 2016, Strome signed a two-year, $6.2 million contract extension to stay with the Oilers. He played parts of two seasons with the Oilers. On November 16, 2018, the Oilers traded Strome to the New York Rangers in exchange for Ryan Spooner. On November 6, 2020, Strome signed a two-year contract to stay with the Rangers. They defeated the Buffalo Sabres, Montreal Canadiens, and New Jersey Devils on their way to the Stanley Cup Finals. In 1989, Lemelin along with his Bruins teammate Andy Moog won the William M. Jennings Trophy for fewest goals scored against in the regular-season. On January 12, 1993, Lemelin decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey. After retiring, Lemelin became the goaltending coach for the Philadelphia Flyers. He served as coach until he was replaced on June 25, 2009.

Rüdiger Schnuphase (born 23 January 1954) is a former German footballer. He played as a midfielder for FC Rot-Weiß Erfurt and FC Carl Zeiss Jena, and was capped 45 times for East Germany. He notably played for East Germany at the 1974 FIFA World Cup and the 1980 Summer Olympics.

Rüstü Erdogan (* 3 August 2006) is an Austrian football player. Erdogan began his career at FC Red Bull Salzburg. From the 2020/21 season onward, he went through all age groups in the Red Bull academy. For the 2024/25 season, he joined the squad of the second-division team, FC Liefering.[1] Due to injury, he missed the autumn season. In January 2025 which he was loaned to the regional league club SK Bischofshofen in January 2025 on a cooperative basis. In March 2025 he made his debut for Bischofshofen in the Regionalliga West. In April 2025 Erdogan made his debut for Liefering in the second division. He came as substitute for Marc Striednig in the 83rd minute of the 22nd matchday against SV Horn. Rıdvan Bolatlı (2 December 1928 – 31 March 2022) was a Turkish professional footballer. He played in Turkey for Ankaragücü. He was born in Ankara. Bolatlı made six appearances for the Turkey national team from 1953 until 1954.

Saara Sofia Aalto (born 2 May 1987) is a Finnish singer. She was the runner-up of both The Voice of Finland in 2011 and The X Factor UK in 2016. She also represented Finland at the Eurovision Song Contest 2018 with the song "Monsters" and finished in 25th place. She is a celebrity judge on the Finnish X Factor and was a contestant on Dancing on Ice in 2019.
Sabah Abdul-Jalil (1 July 1951 – 28 February 2021) was an Iraqi footballer and manager. He last coached Al-Quwa Al-Jawiya. Abdul-Jalil died on 28 February 2021 from COVID-19 in Baghdad, aged 69.
Sabbineni Meghana (born 7 June 1996) is a cricketer from India. She plays for two teams, Railways and India, and is mainly a right-handed batter. She has previously played for Andhra and South Zone.

Sabah Bizi (13 November 1946 – 16 January 2025) was an Albanian footballer. He played for Vllaznia Shkodër and Partizani Tirana as well as the Albania national team. He played for the national team from 1967 to 1976, making fifteen appearances. Bizi died on 16 January 2025, at the age of 78.

Sabine Lisicki (; born 22 September 1989 in Troisdorf) is a German professional tennis player. Lisicki won her first WTA title match in more than three seasons in Hong Kong in September 2014. She reached her high rank of world no. 12 on 21 May 2012 in singles.
Sabine Kottig is a German water polo player. She was part of the German women's national water polo team at the 2003 World Aquatics Championships and 2001 Women's European Water Polo Championship.

Sabine Schmitz (; 14 May 1969 – 16 March 2021) was a German professional motor racing driver and television personality. She was known for racing BMW and Porsche. She also appeared on BBC's Top Gear, making many appearances alongside several of the programme's presenters. In 2017, Schmitz was diagnosed with cancer. She died from the disease on 16 March 2021 at a hospital in Trier, Germany at the age of 51.

Sabine Brehm (born 5 May 1963) is a East-German long track speed skater. She represented her country at international competitions until 1987. She won the bronze medal at the 1985 World Allround Speed Skating Championships for Women in Sarajevo, and 1986 World Allround Speed Skating Championships for Women in Den Haag. She also won the bronze allround medal at the 1985 European Speed Skating Championships for Women in Groningen. Brehm won at the 1984 national championships the 3000m. She set two national records in 1985 and during her career a total of 8 track records.

Sabina Luciani (born 18 June 1963) is a Danish taekwondo athlete. She competed at the 1988 Summer Olympics, where taekwondo was a demonstration sport, in the welterweight event. At the 1988 European Taekwondo Championships she won the bronze medal in the -65 kg category.

Saber Eid Ali Omar (; (1 May 1959 – 29 December 2025) was an Egyptian footballer. He played 14 times for the Egypt national team, and was part of their team at the 1990 FIFA World Cup. Eid was diagnosed with lung cancer, and had tumors in his leg and in his lung. He died on 29 December 2025.

Eid Sabbit Dudu Damor (; 1930 – 28 September 2022), commonly known as Sabit Dudu, was a Sudanese footballer. He played for Sudan at the 1959 and 1963 African Cup of Nations. Dudu started playing football as a forward, before becoming a goalkeeper. He played for Al Hilal Omdurman for 14 years between 1953 and 1967, before retiring from football because of an injury. After he retired, he worked as a goalkeeper coach at Al-Ahli Jeddah. Dudu died on 28 September 2022.

Saburo Kawabuchi is a former Japanese football player and manager. He played for the Japan national team. He also managed the Japan national team. Kawabuchi was born in Takaishi on December 3, 1936. After graduating from Waseda University, he played for Furukawa Electric. In 1965, Furukawa Electric joined new league Japan Soccer League. In the initial league season, he was the first player to score a hat-trick, against Nagoya Mutual Bank. He retired in 1970. He played 68 games and scored 10 goals in the league. On December 25, 1958, when Kawabuchi was a Waseda University student, he debuted and scored 2 goals for the Japan national team against Hong Kong. In 1962, he played at 1962 Asian Games. In 1964, he was selected Japan for 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. At 1964 Summer Olympics, he scored a goal in first match against Argentina. He also played at 1962 Asian Games. He played 26 games and scored 8 goals for Japan until 1965. After retirement, Kawabuchi became a coach for Furukawa Electric in 1970. In 1973, he became a manager and managed until 1975. Just before 1982 World Cup qualification in December 1980, he was named manager for the Japan national team to replace Masashi Watanabe, who suffered a subarachnoid hemorrhage. Kawabuchi managed Japan at 1982 World Cup qualification and managed until March 1981. In 1991, he named inaugural chairman of the J.League is first professional league in Japan. In 1991, he also became a first chairman of J.League. In 2002, he resigned chairman of J.League and became 10th president of Japan Football Association as Shunichiro Okano successor. Kawabuchi served until 2008. He also served as president of Japan Basketball Association from May 2015 to June 2016. In 2006, he received FIFA Order of Merit. In 2008, he was also selected Japan Football Hall of Fame.

Terry Michael Brunk (December 12, 1964 – May 11, 2025) was an American professional wrestler. He was better known by his ring name Sabu. He is best known for working with Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW), Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), and World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) on their ECW brand. He was known for competing in hardcore-type matches. He was trained by his uncle, Ed Farhat who was known by his ring name, The Sheik. On November 5, 2021, Sabu announced that he was retiring from wrestling. He would come out of retirement at All Elite Wrestling's Double or Nothing pay-per-view in 2023. On April 18, 2025, Sabu wrestled his last match at Game Changer Wrestling’s Joey Janela's Spring Break 9. He died weeks later on May 11, 2025 at the age of 60. Sabrina Bulleri (7 January 1959 - 18 April 2000, Ghezzano) was an Italian Paralympic athlete. She won bronze medals at the 1984 Summer Paralympics, in the 4x400 meters, and 100 meters. She won gold medals at the 1988 Summer Paralympic Games in the 4x100 meters, 200 meters, and 100 meters. She won a bronze medal at the 4x200 meters. Sabrina Bulleri started practicing sports in the ASHA company of Pisa, where she trained with Soriano Ceccanti, Mariella Bertini and Santo Mangano, all of whom became Paralympic champions. She competed in category 3 (wheelchair athletes), emerging in speed races, where, at the Seoul Paralympics, she won three gold medals, in the 100, 200 meters, and in the 4 × 100 meters relay. She also won three bronze medals. After 1990, she left the competitive sport. After a long illness, she died in April 2000 in Ghezzano. Sachin Ramesh Tendulkar (born 24 April 1973 in Mumbai) is a former Indian cricketer. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest batsman in the history of cricket. He has the highest number of runs in both Test cricket and One Day Internationals. He also has the highest number of centuries in the Test Cricket format. He always honoured better players than him like Garfield Sobers or Don Bradman. Sachin Tendulkar is one of the richest cricketers of India. Tendulkar scored his much awaited 100th international hundred on 16 March 2012 against Bangladesh in the Asia Cup. He became the first person in history to achieve this feat. Incidentally, it was Tendulkar's first ODI hundred against Bangladesh. He said "It's been a tough phase for me... I was not thinking about the milestone, the media started all this, wherever I went, the restaurant, room service, everyone was talking about the 100th hundred. Nobody talked about my 99 hundreds. It became mentally tough for me because nobody talked about my 99 hundreds." 1994 - Arjuna Award, by the Government of India in recognition of his outstanding achievement in sports. 1997-98 - Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, India's highest honour given for achievement in sports. 1999 - Padma Shri, India's 'fourth' highest civilian award. 2001 - Maharashtra Bhushan Award, Maharashtra State's highest Civilian Award. 2008 - Padma Vibhushan, India's second highest civilian award. 2014 - Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.

Sachi Kagawa was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Kagawa was born in Hiroshima Prefecture. He played for his local club Rijo Shukyu-Dan. He won 1924 and 1925 Emperor's Cup with international players Naoemon Shimizu and Shizuo Miyama. In May 1925, Kagawa was selected the Japan national team for Far Eastern Championship Games in Manila. At this competition, on May 17, he debuted against Philippines. On May 20, he also played against Republic of China. But Japan lost in both matches (0-4, v Philippines and 0-2, v Republic of China). He played 2 games for Japan in 1925.

Saburo Shinosaki was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Shinosaki played for Keio University. He won the 1937 Emperor's Cup. He also played for Keio BRB which was consisted of his alma mater Keio University players and graduates. He won the 1939 and 1940 Emperor's Cup at the club with Yukio Tsuda, Hirokazu Ninomiya and Takashi Kasahara. 1940 Emperor's Cup was the last Emperor's Cup before the war because Emperor's Cup was suspended for World War II from 1941 to 1945. On June 16, 1940, when Shinosaki was a Keio University student, he debuted for Japan national team against Philippines and Japan won the match. This match was the first match since 1936 Summer Olympics and the only match in the 1940s in Japan's "International A Match" due to World War II.

Sachiko Honda (本田幸子, December 30, 1930 - May 1st, 2020) is a female 8-dan Japanese professional Go player at Nihon Ki-in. The Mukai sisters (Kozue, Chiaki, Kaori) are her pupils, and all of them are professional players. She also has two sisters: Kazuko Sugiuchi (Older sister, mentor of Tomoko Kato) and Teruko Kusunoki (Younger sister), both of them are professional players.

Sachiko Hara (原幸子) is a Japanese professional Go player at Nihon Ki-in. She is well known about her promotion activities for this game. Her husband is Norimoto Yoda, a 9 dan professional Go player who has obtained many titles including the grand master (名人) title. She is managing a Go school (Yodajuku, 依田塾) with him for kids under 15.

Sacha Boisvert (born March 17, 2006) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Boisvert played two seasons with the Muskegon Lumberjacks of United States Hockey League (USHL), one year with North Dakota Fighting Hawks of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC), and one year with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the USHL All-Rookie Second Team in 2023 and the All-USHL Third Team in 2024. He was also named the NCHC Rookie of the Year and was named to the All-NCHC Rookie Team in 2025. He was drafted 18th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On March 16, 2026, he signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. On March 26, Boisvert made his NHL debut in a 5–1 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. On April 4, Boisvert scored his first NHL goal against Philipp Grubauer in a 4–2 win against the Seattle Kraken.

Sadaharu Oh, also known as Wang Chenchih, is a Japanese-Chinese professional athlete. He is best known as a baseball player and manager. Oh was born in Tokyo. He is the son of a Chinese father and a Japanese mother. Although Oh has always lived in Japan, he has never allowed a loss of his Chinese citizenship. Oh played for the Yomiuri Giants. In 1977, he set the world record for home runs. Oh retired from playing in 1980. From 1984 to 1988, he was the Giants' manager. He managed the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks from 1995 to 2008. In 2006, he was the manager of the Japanese national team in the World Baseball Classic.

Sadio Mané (born 10 April 1992) is a Senegalese professional footballer. He plays for Saudi Pro League club Al Nassr and the Senegal national team. He plays as a winger. He was born in Sédhiou. In 2011, Mané came from Génération Foot to FC Metz in France. He played for the youth teams and the second team. His first game in the first team was on 24 January 2012 against SC Bastia. In 2012, he moved to Austria. There he played for Red Bull Salzburg in the Austrian Bundesliga. He won the Austrian Bundesliga and Austrian Cup in 2014 with Salzburg. In 2015, he moved to Premier League club Southampton. In 2015, Mané set a new Premier League record for the fastest hat-trick. He scored three times in 176 seconds (two minutes and 56 seconds) during a 6–1 win over Aston Villa. Mané signed for Liverpool in 2016 for a fee of £34 million. At the time, this made him the most expensive African player in history. In his second season with Liverpool, he scored in the 2018 UEFA Champions League Final in his side's 3–1 loss to Real Madrid. This made him the first Senegalese to score in the final of the competition. The next season, Mané won the 2018–19 UEFA Champions League with Liverpool, defeating Tottenham Hotspur 2–0 in the final. The same season, he was the joint-winner of the Premier League Golden Boot with 22 goals. During the 2019–20 season, Mané scored two goals in the UEFA Super Cup against Chelsea as Liverpool won on penalties. He also played in the Liverpool's first FIFA Club World Cup final win. In January 2020, he was named CAF African Footballer of the Year. Liverpool went on to win the club's first Premier League title, and first league title since 1990, at the end of the season. Mané has played for the Senegalese national team since 2012. He has played 60 times and scored 16 goals for the national side. He has played for Senegal at the 2012 Summer Olympics, 2015 Africa Cup of Nations, 2017 Africa Cup of Nations and the 2018 FIFA World Cup. Sadie Anderson (born 25 May 1990) is an American rugby union player. She played for the United States women's national rugby union team at the 2014 Women's Rugby World Cup. She played for Pennsylvania State University.

Safyaan Mohammed Sharif is a cricketer from Scotland. He plays for the Scotland national cricket team. He was born on May 24, 1991 and his role is bowler.

Sahibzada Muhammad Hamid Raza, is a Pakistani politician who is member-elect of the National Assembly of Pakistan. Raza won the 2024 Pakistani general election from NA-104 Faisalabad-X as an Independent candidate. He received 128,687 votes while runner up Daniyal Ahmed of Pakistan Muslim League (N) (PML (N)) received 92,594 votes.
Sahib Khazal (1 January 1943 – 9 May 2025) was an Iraqi footballer. He played for Iraq at the 1972 AFC Asian Cup. Khazal died in Baghdad on 9 May 2025, at the age of 82.

Said Nišić (born 5 May 2008 in Sarajevo, Bosnia and Herzegovina) is a Bosnian footballer. He plays as forward for the Austrian 2nd league team FC Liefering. Nišić began his career at FK Sarajevo. In October 2021, he moved to Austria to join the youth setup at SV Wals-Grünau. 2022 he went on to FC Red Bull Salzburg. There he progressed through all the academy age groups starting from the 2022/23 season. In April 2025 he was part of the squad for FC Lieferingb for the first time. He made his professional debut in the 2. Liga in May 2026, coming on as a substitute for Oghenetejiri Adejenughure in the 75th minute during the Matchday 28 match against Kapfenberg in the 2025/26 season. Nišić first played for a Bosnian youth national team in September 2022. In November 2025, at the age of 17, he made his debut for the Bosnian U-19 team.

Saiko Takahashi is a former Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Takahashi was born in Osaka Prefecture on April 11, 1976. After graduating from Nishiyama High School, she joined Nikko Securities Dream Ladies in 1995. The club won Nadeshiko League championship for 3 years in a row (1996-1998). However, the club was disbanded in 1998 due to financial strain. She moved to OKI FC Winds in 1999. However the club was disbanded end of 1999 season and she moved to Urawa Reinas FC (later Urawa Reds) in 2000. She was selected Best Eleven in 2004. She retired end of 2009 season. On March 29, 2005, when Takahashi was 28 years old, she debuted for the Japan national team against Australia. She played 2 games for Japan in 2005.

Saina Nehwal (born March 17, 1990) is an Indian female athlete. She is best known as a badminton player who competed in the Summer Olympic Games. Saina won a bronze medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London. SAINA NEHWAL was awarded the Arjuna Award in 2009 and a year later, the Government of India honoured her with the Padma Shri, the fourth highest civilian honour in India. In 2009, Nehwal was honoured with India’s highest award for sporting excellence - the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award. In 2016, the Government of India awarded Saina Nehwal the Padma Bhushan. It is the 3rd highest civilian honour in the country. She became the first Indian badminton player to win a BWF Series event and continued to impress on her way to winning the gold medal at the Commonwealth Games in 2010. In 2015, Saina Nehwal won the singles event at the India Open BWF Super Series and became the number 1 women’s player in the Badminton World Federation rankings.

Sajid Iqbal Mahmood (born 21 December 1981 in Bolton, Greater Manchester) is an English cricketer of Pakistani Janjua Rajput descent. He is a right-arm fast bowler who plays international cricket for England and county cricket for Lancashire.

Sakae Takahashi was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Takahashi played for Osaka SC which many Japan national team players Yoshimatsu Oyama, Toshio Miyaji, Uichiro Hatta and Kiyonosuke Marutani were playing in those days. In May 1925, Takahashi was selected the Japan national team for Far Eastern Championship Games in Manila. At this competition, on May 20, he debuted against Republic of China. But Japan lost in this match (0-2).

Saizo Saito was a Japanese football player. He played for the Japan national team. Saito was born in Osaka Prefecture on September 24, 1908. He played for Kwangaku Club which was consisted of his alma mater Kwansei Gakuin University players and graduates. At the club, he won 1929 Emperor's Cup with Yukio Goto, Hideo Sakai and so on. In May 1930, when Saito was a Kwansei Gakuin University student, he was selected the Japan national team for Far Eastern Championship Games in Tokyo and Japan won the championship. At this competition, on May 25, he debuted against Philippines. On May 29, he also played against Republic of China. He played 2 games for Japan in 1930. After graduating from Kwansei Gakuin University, Saito retired playing career and want to England and studied football at University of Bristol. In 1933, he joined Osaka Mainichi Shimbun and he was engaged in the management and reporting of All Japan High School Soccer Tournament until 1940. After that, he worked at Hino Motors and some affiliates until 1989. He also served as the president at some Hino Motors affiliates. Saito died in 2004.

Sakahoko Nobushige (born as Yoshiaki Fukuzono; 18 June 1961 – 16 September 2019) was a Japanese sumo wrestler. His highest rank was sekiwake. He later became the head coach of Izutsu stable. He was the elder brother of Terao Tsunefumi. Nobushige was born in Kagoshima, Japan. Sakahoko made his professional debut in January 1978. Sakahoko died of pancreatic cancer on 16 September 2019 at the age of 58.

Sakai (Japanese: 坂井, 酒井 etc) is a Japanese surname. It has many kanji descriptions. Things with this name include: Yuki Sakai (footballer, born 1989), not to be confused with Yuki Sakai (footballer, born 1985)

Saku Antero Koivu (born November 23, 1974 in Turku, Finland) is a former Finnish professional ice hockey player and an alternate captain of the Anaheim Ducks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He began his NHL career with the Montreal Canadiens in 1995–96 after three seasons with TPS of the Finnish SM-liiga. Koivu served as the Canadiens' captain for nine of his thirteen seasons with the club (not including the locked-out 2004–05 season), which makes his the second longest captaincy tenure in team history after Jean Béliveau. Koivu was the first European to captain the Montreal Canadiens. On September 6, 2001, Koivu was diagnosed with Burkitt's lymphoma, a non-Hodgkin's lymphoma and he nearly all of the 2001–02 season. After he had been suffering serious pains in his stomach and was vomiting went to see the Canadiens' physician David Mulder, who, after many tests discovered the cancer. He was expected to miss the season but he made a comeback in time for the last few games. The fans gave Koivu an eight-minute standing ovation when he skated onto the Molson Centre ice for the first time on April 9, 2002. For both his courage and his off-ice team leadership while he was undergoing cancer treatment, Koivu was awarded the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy following the 2002 playoffs. Saki Kumagai is a Japanese footballer. She plays for the Japan national team. Kumagai was born in Sapporo on October 17, 1990. After graduating from Tokiwagi Gakuen High School, she joined for Urawa Reds in 2009. The club won Nadeshiko League championship in 2009 season. In July 2011, she moved to German Bundesliga club Frankfurt. After she played 2 season, she moved to French Division 1 Feminine club Olympique Lyonnais in June 2013. Kumagai scored the decisive penalty for Lyon in the 2016 UEFA Champions League Final, following a player-of-the-match performance. On March 7, 2008, when Kumagai was 17 years old, she debuted for the Japan national team against Canada. In August, Kumagai was selected for the Japan U-20 national team at the 2008 U-20 World Cup. In 2010, she played for the U-20 team as captain during the 2010 U-20 World Cup. In 2011, she was part of Japan's World Cup-winning team, scoring the winning penalty in the final against the United States. She was also in the squad at the 2012 Summer Olympics and the 2015 World Cup. Japan came second at both competitions. In January 2017, she was named Japan's captain by manager Asako Takakura. In 2018, Japan won the 2018 Asian Cup. She has played more than 100 games for Japan. On November 10, 2019, Kumagai scored her first ever goal in a friendly match for Japan in a 2–0 win against South Africa.

Salah Assad (; born 13 March 1958) is an Algerian former football player and manager who played as a forward. Known for his agility and precise finishing, Assad played a crucial role in leading Algeria to their stunning victory against West Germany, assisting one of the goals in their iconic 2-1 win. His tenacity and flair on the field, combined with his ability to find the back of the net, made him a standout performer. Assad's exceptional play and tactical awareness were instrumental in Algeria's impressive debut at the world stage, capturing the hearts of fans globally and leaving an indelible mark on the tournament's history. Widely considered as one of the best left-wingers in African football history. He made his debut in adult football in 1975 with Raed Shabab Cuba, in which he spent seven seasons and helped the team become the champion of Algeria in 1981. During the 1982–83 season, he defended the colors of the French Mulhouse, but at the end of the season, the club took the last 20th place and was relegated from the elite division, after which Assad moved to Paris Saint-Germain. He played for the Parisian team the next season of his playing career, but could not gain a foothold in the main team. In 1984, he returned to the Mulhouse club, which continued to play in the second division. This time he spent two seasons in the team and scored quite regularly, but the team in both seasons occupied only second place in its group and could not return to the top division. In the summer of 1986, he returned to his native club Raed Shabab Cuba, for which he played another 4 seasons. He finished his professional career as a football player playing for this club in 1990. In 1978, he made his debut in official matches as part of the Algerian national team. In the same year, as part of the national team, he won gold medals at the All-African Games in Algeria, scoring one goal. In 1980, he played as part of the Algerian national team at the Olympic football tournament in the USSR, where the "desert foxes" were able to get out of the group. As a member of the national team, he participated in the 1980 African Cup of Nations in Nigeria, where he won silver with the team, the 1982 African Cup of Nations, the 1982 World Cup in Spain and the 1986 World Cup in Mexico. During his career in the national team, which lasted 12 years, he spent 68 matches in the uniform of the main team of the country, scoring 15 goals. For the minor league baseball team, see Salem Witches (baseball). The Salem Witch Trials (1692-1693) were a series of witch trials in the Massachusetts Bay Colony. This was the biggest witch hunt ever to occur in New England. Many similar witch hunts, trials and executions were carried out in Britain and elsewhere. The first accusations of witchcraft happened in January 1692. The trials began the following month in February. They took place in county courts in Essex, Suffolk and Middlesex Counties of colonial Massachusetts. By May 1693, when the trials finally ended, more than 200 people had been accused of practicing witchcraft. Over 150 of them had been jailed, 20 had been executed (one by torture), and at least 5 died in prison. Eventually, several of the accusers (mostly teenage girls) admitted that their testimony and accusations were false. Today, the trials are often viewed as examples of mass hysteria and moral panic. At this time, most New Englanders thought that witches truly existed and were a real and constant danger. Their ideas about witchcraft were closely tied to their religious beliefs: Most ministers in New England believed that all magic was diabolical, and that witches received powers from the Devil to [control] the weather, cause illness, destroy crops, and harm livestock. [They believed] witches made a covenant with the Devil that was similar to the covenant [that] church members made, and they deserved to be punished with death because... they were “enemies to God, and all true religion.” The threat of witchcraft was believed to be particularly menacing in New England due to the special mission of Puritan colonists to create a godly society.New Englanders believed that witches could look and act just like normal people - which meant any normal person could be accused of witchcraft. The Salem trials were not the only ones to occur in New England in the 1600s. During the 17th century, fourteen other women and two men were executed for witchcraft in the Massachusetts Bay Colony and Connecticut Colony At the time, many Puritans lived in Salem, Masssachusetts. In 1689, the preacher Samuel Parris was made the leader of this community. In his sermons, he often talked about the struggle between the chosen people of God and Satan. In 1691 and 1692 his daughter Elizabeth ("Betty"), his niece Abigail, and two other children started to act and speak strangely. They also tried to hide under things and crawl on the floor. Parris consulted several doctors, but none of them had a medical explanation for the behaviour. A doctor called William Griggs also examined the girls. After ruling out the mental illnesses known at the time, he suggested that they could be possessed by the Devil. He thought the devil was making them move in strange ways. Abigail and Elizabeth later confirmed this and said that invisible hands were vexing them. Elizabeth claimed that Satan had approached her, and because she refused him, he was sending out his servants: the witches. Parris took this as confirmation that the Devil was possessing the children. He announced that the city was occupied by the Devil, and that an army of small devils was ready to invade. The villagers, who were often threatened by Native Americans, believed the accusations. Parris believed that to fight the Devil, each and every witch in Salem had to be identified and named. Elizabeth, Abigail, and a few other children began naming witches. The first three people they accused were socially disadvantaged people on the edge of society. Sarah Good, a well-known beggar and the daughter of a pub-owner Tituba, one of Samuel Parris' slaves, probably an Arawak from Guyana The trials began after a few local women in Salem Village were accused of witchcraft by four young girls, Betty Parris (9), Abigail Williams (11), Ann Putnam Jr. (12), and Elizabeth Hubbard (17). The girls twisted themselves into strange shapes, screamed, and spoke meaningless words. A doctor concluded that witches had invaded Salem Village and were bewitching the girls. Tituba, an enslaved woman, was blamed and became the first person to be accused of witchcraft. A woman named Bridget Bishop was the next to be accused, and was the first to be executed. Soon there was a core group of accusers, all girls and young women between the ages of 9 and 20. According to a 2025 article by Sarah Pruitt:[They] screamed, writhed, barked and displayed other horrifying symptoms they claimed were signs of Satanic possession... [The accusers] included members of [important] village families, as well as domestic servants and refugees of King William’s War, a long-running conflict that pitted English settlers against the indigenous Wabanaki people and their French allies. Often, the accusers claimed a witch was injuring or sickening them. For example, when 16-year-old Mary Daniel testified in court that Margret Scott was bewitching her, she said:I was taken very ill again all over & felt a great pricking in [the] soles of my feet, and after a while I saw apparently the shape of Margret Scott, who, as I was sitting in a chair by [the] fire pulled me with [the] chair, down backward to [the] ground, and tormented and pinched me very much.These symptoms may have been caused by mass hysteria. In April 1692, a young woman accused Reverend George Burroughs of witchcraft. (Burroughs was a Harvard graduate who had been a minister in Salem Village in the early 1680s before moving back to Maine.) According to a 2024 research guide by Tricia Peone: One of the [accusers] testified that she had seen “the Apparition of a Minister who confessed to murdering and bewitching people and claimed to be a “conjurer.” In a sinister reversal of the minister’s role, he commanded her to sign her name in his book and give her soul to the Devil. His accusers identified him as the leader of all the witches in northern New England, and their testimonies [claimed he committed] other mockeries of Puritan faith such as holding a sabbath in Rev. Parris’ pasture, taking a sacrament of blood, and [allowing] women (witches) as deacons. Burroughs was unable to convince the court or his fellow ministers that he was a minister of God and not of the Devil.Burroughs was executed for witchcraft on August 19, 1692. The Salem Witch Trials involved two kinds of trials. First, court hearings were held before local magistrates; then trials were held in county court. The trials were held in Salem, and accused witches from surrounding areas were brought to Salem to be tried for witchcraft. The best-known trials were held by the Court of Oyer and Terminer in 1692 in Salem Town. All twenty-six people who went to trial before this court were convicted. In 1693, there were also four sessions of the Superior Court of Judicature in Salem. During these court sessions, thirty-one accused witches were tried for practicing witchcraft, but only three were convicted. Sometimes, "trials" that sentenced people to death lasted just 15 minutes. During the Trials, over 150 people accused of witchcraft were arrested and put in jail. Even more people were accused, but were never formally charged by the authorities. Most of the accused were women. 29 people were found guilty of witchcraft, which was a capital felony, punishable by death 19 of these people (14 women and 5 men) were hanged on Gallows Hill in present-day Salem, Massachusetts At least 5 accused witches died in prison Another (Giles Corey) was crushed to death under heavy stones after he refused to plead guilty or not guilty By late 1692, the trials had gotten so out of control that the accusers began to accuse prominent and well-connected individuals, including the wife of Governor William Phips. After this shift in targets, people began to think about the proceedings more critically. Increase Mather, a respected minister, published "Cases of Conscience Concerning Evil Spirits," where he questioned whether spectral evidence was really reliable. This type of evidence had been central to the Salem convictions. Historians have proposed many explanations for Salem's sudden witch panic. The accusers may have been impacted by any of these factors: Rebellion against strict gender roles (children, especially girls, were to be seen and not heard) Family rivalries (some accusers might have been pressured to accuse members of opposing families) According to the Salem Witch Museum: "Perhaps the main reason for witchcraft accusations in 1692 Topsfield were generations-long border disputes with Salem Village." However, many other factors may have contributed, including: Ergotism (a condition caused by a fungus that grows on rye and other grains) A large increase in refugees from King William's War

Salma Celeste Paralluelo Ayingono (born 13 November 2003) is a Spanish footballer and former sprinter. She is known for her achievements in both track and field events and football. Paralluelo plays as a left winger for FC Barcelona in the Liga F league and represents the Spain women's national football team. Salma Celeste Paralluelo Ayingono was born in Zaragoza, Spain. Her father is Spanish, and her mother is from Equatorial Guinea. Her mother moved to Spain to get better medical treatment for her son from a previous relationship who had a severe congenital vision deficiency. This move allowed Salma's family to receive medical support for her brother's condition. Apart from her brother, she also has two more brothers, José Jaime and Lorenzo, both of whom are footballers. Paralluelo's sporting journey began in athletics. She joined the San José Athletics club in Zaragoza and later the Scorpio-71 club in Zaragoza. She quickly gained attention in the athletics world. In 2019, she won a bronze medal at the Spanish Indoor Athletics Championships in the 400-meter event, setting a Spanish national record for her age category. Paralluelo's talents extended beyond athletics. She also excelled in football. She started her football career with UD San José in Zaragoza and played for Zaragoza CFF and Villarreal in Spain. After her contract with Villarreal ended, she signed with FC Barcelona at the end of the 2021/22 season. Salma Paralluelo achieved remarkable success in international competitions. She won the 2018 UEFA Women's Under-17 Championship, the 2018 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, and the 2022 FIFA U-20 Women's World Cup with the Spanish national teams. She made her senior debut for the Spain women's national football team on 11 November 2022, scoring a hat-trick in a friendly match against Argentina. Notably, Paralluelo was a nominee for the 2022 FIFA Puskás Award, recognizing outstanding goals in football. In the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup, Paralluelo was a key player for the Spain women's national team. She scored crucial goals in the quarter-final and semi-final matches, helping Spain reach the World Cup final for the first time in history. On 15 August 2023, she scored a goal in Spain's 2–1 victory over Sweden, contributing to her team's journey to the World Cup final.
